chunks: These two (believers and unbelievers) are disputants, who contend about their Lord. But they who disbelieve will be fitted out with garments of flames. Boiling water will be poured down over their heads

key_terms.خَصْمَانِ: Two disputants/parties in a legal or cosmic contest

ai.seo_question: What is the specific punishment described for disbelievers in Surah Al-Hajj regarding garments of fire and boiling water?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as the initial stage of the 'Khuzm' (the first blow) on the Day of Judgment, where the disbelievers are clad in garments of fire, symbolizing the external manifestation of their internal rejection. The pouring of boiling water (Al-Hamim) over their heads serves as a precursor to the final punishment in Hellfire, emphasizing the physical reality of divine retribution for those who disputed the truth of their Lord. This imagery underscores the concept of 'Tazkiyah' (purification) through suffering, distinguishing the fate of the disbelievers from the believers who will be gathered under the banner of the Ahl al-Bayt.
